table.name: circuits
table.purpose: F1 circuits reference table: one row per racing circuit, with location and geographic coordinates. Referenced by races (each race is held at a circuit).

col_001.name: circuitId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each circuit.

col_002.name: circuitRef
col_002.description: Unique slug/reference code for the circuit (lowercase, URL-friendly), e.g. 'ricard', 'zolder'.

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Full display name of the circuit, e.g. 'Circuit Paul Ricard', 'Silverstone Circuit'.

col_004.name: location
col_004.description: City/town or locality where the circuit is situated, e.g. 'Le Castellet', 'Heusden-Zolder'.

col_006.name: lat
col_006.description: Latitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -34.9 to 57.3).

col_007.name: lng
col_007.description: Longitude of the circuit in decimal degrees (range -118.2 to 138.9).

col_009.name: url
col_009.description: Wikipedia URL for the circuit's page.

table.name: constructorResults
table.purpose: Per-race championship points earned by each constructor (Formula 1). One row per constructor per race; points feed constructorStandings.

col_001.name: constructorResultId
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying each constructor-per-race result row.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to the race (races table) in which the constructor scored these points. 907 distinct races, matching the races/results tables.

col_003.name: constructorId
col_003.description: Reference to the constructor (team) that scored the points; joins to constructors.col_001. 172 distinct constructors.

col_004.name: points
col_004.description: Championship points scored by the constructor in that race (0–66; 0 most common).

col_005.name: status
col_005.description: Result status flag; only value 'D' (17 rows, ~0.2% non-null), indicating the constructor was disqualified from that race. Null otherwise.

table.name: constructorStandings
table.purpose: Formula 1 constructor (team) championship standings after each race: one row per constructor per race, with cumulative points, championship position, and win count at that point in the season.

col_001.name: constructorStandingsId
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying each standings row.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to races.col_001; the race after which the standings were computed.

col_003.name: constructorId
col_003.description: Reference to constructors.col_001; the team whose standing this row records.

col_004.name: points
col_004.description: Cumulative championship points for the constructor at that race; can be fractional (e.g. 27.5, 72.5) due to shared points or half-point races.

col_005.name: position
col_005.description: Numeric championship position of the constructor after that race (1-22).

col_006.name: positionText
col_006.description: Position rendered as text (same values as col_005); stored as VARCHAR.

col_007.name: wins
col_007.description: Number of race wins by the constructor up to and including that race (mostly 0).

table.name: constructors
table.purpose: Formula 1 constructors (racing teams): one row per constructor, with its identifier, name, nationality and Wikipedia URL. Referenced by results, standings, qualifying, lap times and pit stops tables.

col_001.name: constructorId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the constructor, referenced by results, qualifying, standings, lap times and pit stops.

col_002.name: constructorRef
col_002.description: Unique short slug/reference code for the constructor (lowercase, hyphenated, e.g. 'tyrrell', 'cooper-borgward').

col_003.name: name
col_003.description: Full display name of the constructor (e.g. 'Alfa Romeo', 'Brabham-Repco').

col_004.name: nationality
col_004.description: Constructor's nationality as an adjective (British, American, Italian, etc.).

col_005.name: url
col_005.description: Wikipedia URL for the constructor's page.

table.name: driverStandings
table.purpose: Formula 1 driver championship standings after each race: one row per driver per race, showing cumulative points, championship position, and wins to date. Joins to races and drivers.

col_001.name: driverStandingsId
col_001.description: Surrogate primary key, unique per row.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to races.col_001; the race after which the standings were computed. 970 distinct races.

col_003.name: driverId
col_003.description: Reference to drivers.col_001; the driver this standing belongs to.

col_004.name: points
col_004.description: Cumulative championship points for the driver after that race; can be fractional (e.g. 27.5) due to shared/fastest-lap point rules.

col_005.name: position
col_005.description: Championship position (numeric rank) after that race; 1..108, each rank appearing once per race.

col_006.name: positionText
col_006.description: Championship position as text; here identical to col_005 (stored as VARCHAR). In the standard schema this can also hold 'D' for disqualified, though no such value appears in the sample.

col_007.name: wins
col_007.description: Cumulative number of race wins for the driver up to and including that race (0 for most rows).

table.name: drivers
table.purpose: Formula 1 drivers reference table: one row per driver, with identity, birth date, nationality and Wikipedia link. Referenced by results, qualifying, lapTimes, pitStops, driverStandings and constructorResults.

col_001.name: driver_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each driver, referenced by results, qualifying, lapTimes, pitStops, driverStandings, constructorResults.

col_002.name: driver_ref
col_002.description: Unique slug/code identifying the driver (lowercase surname-based, e.g. 'gilles_villeneuve'), used as a textual reference key.

col_003.name: driver_number
col_003.description: Permanent car/race number of the driver (2-99); null for ~96% of rows, mostly older drivers before permanent numbering.

col_004.name: driver_code
col_004.description: Three-letter driver abbreviation (e.g. VER, ROS, SAI) used in timing screens; null for ~90% of rows.

col_008.name: nationality
col_008.description: Driver's nationality as an adjective (British, American, Italian, ...).

col_009.name: url
col_009.description: Wikipedia URL for the driver's page; empty string for one row.

table.name: lapTimes
table.purpose: Per-lap timing for each driver in each Formula 1 race (one row per driver per lap).

col_001.name: raceId
col_001.description: Identifier of the race; references races.col_001. Repeats across many rows because each race has hundreds of lap records.

col_002.name: driverId
col_002.description: Identifier of the driver; references drivers.col_001. 121 distinct drivers matches historical F1 driver count.

col_003.name: lap
col_003.description: Lap number within the race (1..78, e.g. Monaco ~78 laps). Part of the row identity with raceId and driverId.

col_004.name: position
col_004.description: Driver's race position at the end of that lap (1..24, roughly the number of starters).

col_006.name: milliseconds
col_006.description: Lap time in milliseconds; numeric counterpart of col_005 (1:31.255 = 91255).

table.name: pitStops
table.purpose: Formula 1 pit stop records: one row per pit stop made by a driver during a race, with the lap, local time, and stop duration.

col_001.name: raceId
col_001.description: Identifier of the race (references races). Same race appears many times, once per pit stop.

col_002.name: driverId
col_002.description: Identifier of the driver making the pit stop (references drivers).

col_003.name: stop
col_003.description: Pit stop number for that driver in the race (1st, 2nd, ... up to 6).

col_004.name: lap
col_004.description: Lap number on which the pit stop occurred (1-74).

col_005.name: time
col_005.description: Local race time of day (HH:MM:SS) at which the pit stop occurred.

col_006.name: duration
col_006.description: Pit stop duration in seconds (stored as text, e.g. '30.888').

col_007.name: milliseconds
col_007.description: Pit stop duration in milliseconds; equals col_006 * 1000 (e.g. 30888 for 30.888).

table.name: qualifying
table.purpose: Formula 1 qualifying session results: one row per driver per race, with their lap times in each qualifying segment (Q1, Q2, Q3) and final grid position.

col_001.name: qualifyId
col_001.description: Primary key of the qualifying table; unique surrogate identifier for each driver's qualifying entry.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to races.col_001; identifies the race (grand prix weekend) this qualifying result belongs to.

col_003.name: driverId
col_003.description: Reference to drivers.col_001; identifies the driver who set these qualifying times.

col_004.name: constructorId
col_004.description: Reference to constructors.col_001; identifies the team the driver qualified for in this race.

col_005.name: number
col_005.description: Driver's car number for the race (0-99 range, matches F1 car numbers).

col_006.name: position
col_006.description: Final qualifying (grid) position, 1-28, with each position appearing roughly once per race.

col_007.name: q1
col_007.description: Driver's best lap time in qualifying segment Q1, formatted m:ss.mmm; null if no time set.

col_008.name: q2
col_008.description: Driver's best lap time in qualifying segment Q2, formatted m:ss.mmm; null if eliminated in Q1 or no time set (hence ~51% null).

col_009.name: q3
col_009.description: Driver's best lap time in qualifying segment Q3, formatted m:ss.mmm; null if eliminated before Q3 or no time set (hence ~71% null).

table.name: races
table.purpose: One row per Formula 1 Grand Prix race (1950–2017), identified by a race id, with its season, round number, circuit, name, date, scheduled start time, and Wikipedia link. Referenced by results, qualifying, lap times, pit stops and standings tables.

col_001.name: race_id
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the race, referenced by results, qualifying, lapTimes, pitStops, driverStandings, constructorStandings and constructorResults.

col_002.name: year
col_002.description: Season year of the race (1950–2017); matches the season identifier used in results, qualifying and constructorResults.

col_003.name: round
col_003.description: Round number of the race within its season (1–21); each value 1–21 appears 68 times, consistent with one race per round per season.

col_004.name: circuit_id
col_004.description: Foreign key to the circuits table identifying the venue where the race was held (72 distinct circuits).

col_005.name: name
col_005.description: Official name of the Grand Prix, e.g. 'British Grand Prix', 'Monaco Grand Prix'.

col_006.name: date
col_006.description: Race date (YYYY-MM-DD), spanning 1950-05-13 to 2017-11-26; unique per row.

col_007.name: time
col_007.description: Scheduled race start time (HH:MM:SS), presumably local or UTC; null for 75% of rows, mostly older races. Exact timezone basis is not evidenced.

col_008.name: url
col_008.description: Wikipedia URL of the race article, unique per race.

table.name: results
table.purpose: Formula 1 race results: one row per driver per race, with grid position, finishing position, points, laps completed, finishing time/gap, fastest-lap data and finishing status. This is the standard Ergast F1 database 'results' table.

col_001.name: resultId
col_001.description: Primary key of the results table; unique surrogate id for one driver's result in one race.

col_002.name: raceId
col_002.description: Reference to races table; identifies which race this result belongs to.

col_003.name: driverId
col_003.description: Reference to drivers table; identifies the driver of this result.

col_004.name: constructorId
col_004.description: Reference to constructors table; identifies the team the driver raced for in this race.

col_005.name: number
col_005.description: Driver's car number for the race (0-208, mostly small numbers; 0 used when no number).

col_006.name: grid
col_006.description: Starting grid position (0 = started from pit lane, values up to 34).

col_007.name: position
col_007.description: Official finishing position as a number; null (~44.5%) when the driver did not finish (retired/did not classify).

col_008.name: positionText
col_008.description: Finishing position as text: numeric string for classified finishers, 'R' for retired, 'F' and similar codes for other non-finishes (e.g. disqualified/excluded).

col_009.name: positionOrder
col_009.description: Finishing position as a dense ordinal (1..39) with all finishers ordered, used for ranking including non-classified drivers.

col_010.name: points
col_010.description: Championship points scored in this race (0-50; 0 for most rows, 25 for a win, half points and sprint values appear).

col_011.name: laps
col_011.description: Number of laps completed by the driver in this race (0-200).

col_012.name: time
col_012.description: Finishing time or gap to the winner as text, e.g. '+24.160' or '+8:22.19'; null for winner and non-finishers.

col_013.name: milliseconds
col_013.description: Finishing time in milliseconds (1.47M-15.09M ms ≈ 25 min - 4.2 h); null for non-finishers.

col_014.name: fastestLap
col_014.description: Lap number on which the driver set their fastest lap (2-78); null for most rows (recorded only in recent seasons).

col_015.name: rank
col_015.description: Rank of the driver's fastest lap within the race (0-24, 0 = no valid fastest lap); null where fastest-lap data is absent.

col_016.name: fastestLapTime
col_016.description: Fastest lap time as text in m:ss.mmm format, e.g. '1:34.091'; null where not recorded.

col_017.name: fastestLapSpeed
col_017.description: Average speed of the fastest lap in km/h (89.5-257.3); null where not recorded.

col_018.name: statusId
col_018.description: Reference to the status lookup table; code for how the driver's race ended (1 = finished, 11 = retired, etc.).

table.name: seasons
table.purpose: Formula 1 championship seasons, one row per year from 1950 to 2017, with a Wikipedia link for each season.

col_001.name: year
col_001.description: Championship season year (1950-2017), primary key of the table.

col_002.name: url
col_002.description: Wikipedia URL of the article about that Formula One season.

table.name: status
table.purpose: F1 race finish/status lookup table: one row per possible race result status code (finished, lapped, retired with reason). Referenced by the results table to describe how each driver's race ended.

col_001.name: statusId
col_001.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier for each status code.

col_002.name: status
col_002.description: Human-readable race outcome/status label, e.g. 'Finished', '+1 Lap' (finished one or more laps behind the leader), or retirement reason such as 'Engine', 'Out of fuel', 'Fuel rig', 'Water pipe'.
